The following are equivalent

and such that the image of <MATH_0006> in <MATH_0007> is <MATH_0008>,
<STRUCT_0003> there exists a reduced algebraic stack <MATH_0009> and a monomorphism
<MATH_0010> such that <MATH_0011> is a singleton
and such that the image of <MATH_0012> in <MATH_0013> is <MATH_0014>,
<STRUCT_0004> there exists an algebraic stack <MATH_0015>, a monomorphism
<MATH_0016>, and a surjective flat morphism
<MATH_0017> where <MATH_0018> is a field such that

<STRUCT_0005>
Moreover, if these conditions hold, then there exists a unique
strictly full subcategory <MATH_0020>
such that <MATH_0021> is a reduced, locally Noetherian algebraic
stack and <MATH_0022> is a singleton which maps to <MATH_0023>
via the map <MATH_0024>.

If <MATH_0001> is as in (1), then
<MATH_0002> is as in (2). (See
Section <REF_0001>
for the notion of the reduction of an algebraic stack.)
Hence (1) implies (2).
It is immediate that (2) implies (1).
The equivalence of (2) and (3) is immediate from
Lemma <REF_0002>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
At this point we've seen the equivalence of (1) -- (3).
Pick a monomorphism <MATH_0003> as in (2).
Note that this implies that <MATH_0004> is fully faithful, see
Lemma <REF_0003>.
Denote <MATH_0005> the essential image of the functor
<MATH_0006>. Then <MATH_0007> is an equivalence and hence
<MATH_0008> is an algebraic stack, see
Algebraic Stacks, Lemma <REF_0004>.
Apply
Lemma <REF_0005>
to get a strictly full subcategory <MATH_0009>
as in the statement of the lemma.
This proves all the statements of the lemma except for uniqueness.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
In order to prove the uniqueness suppose that
<MATH_0010>
and
<MATH_0011>
are two strictly full subcategories as in the statement of the lemma.
Then the projections
<MATH_0012>
are monomorphisms. The algebraic stack in the middle is nonempty by
Lemma <REF_0006>.
Hence the two projections are isomorphisms by
Lemma <REF_0007>
and we win.
